bugs.what: Directional 'get your bearings' distances (e.g. 'three north, three east') often don't correspond to actual room-to-room movement — following them literally repeatedly overshot or looped back to already-visited rooms instead of the target (happened searching for the slag-hound's den and the Rope Larder).

Taking an unattended-but-'watched' item (e.g. the headframe lantern) costs a companion's regard immediately and irreversibly, with no warning that it's treated as real theft rather than a minor scavenging action, even though many similar 'take X (NPC watching: theft)' prompts elsewhere had no apparent consequence when skipped.

The 480-turn playtest limit was reached one room before the actual Hollow Throne, despite following a fairly efficient main-quest path (3 hollows rested, all key items gathered) — for a game whose own text estimates '40-70 turns per hold, fifteen holds' and treats reaching Marrowgate as roughly the midpoint, the true ending is effectively unreachable within a normal single-session turn budget once any meaningful side content is engaged.

confusions: The exact wayfinding needed to reach specific named sub-locations (Rope Larder, flooded quarry/slag-hound den, Gallows Glade) from 'get your bearings' hints was frequently unclear — cardinal directions given didn't reliably map onto the actual room graph.
It was never explicit whether party size is capped; recruiting a 4th companion (Lys) worked with no pushback, so the stated 'as many as will come' was ambiguous about limits until tested.

Distinguishing which NPC dialogue costs reputation/regard outright vs. after a failed skill check wasn't always clear before selecting the option — some 'a hit costs standing' options seemed harsh for what read as a neutral truth-telling action.
suggestions: Add relative exits or a mini-map/'go toward X' auto-path option for wilderness zones instead of relying on error-prone cardinal-direction bearings.
Surface an explicit party-size cap (or confirmation prompt) when recruiting an additional companion.

Either shorten the critical path to a real ending or raise the suggested turn budget for playtesters, since a focused player following main+companion quests still runs out of turns just outside the final throne room.

Give a one-line preview of standing cost before locking in a dialogue choice (some options already do this — make it universal) so players aren't surprised by reputation losses on 'neutral' truth-telling picks.
